blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the magnitude of the vector \(\underline{v}\) and write the direction cosines of \(\underline{v}\): \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do cheezein poochi gayi hain: vector \(\underline{v}\) ki lambai (magnitude) aur us ke direction cosines.
Direction cosines kya hain? Vector x, y aur z axes ke saath jo angles \(\alpha\), \(\beta\), \(\gamma\) banata hai, un ke cosines. Yeh batate hain ke vector kis taraf ishara kar raha hai.
Formula: \(\cos\alpha = x/|\underline{v}|\), \(\cos\beta = y/|\underline{v}|\), \(\cos\gamma = z/|\underline{v}|\).
Plan: pehle \(|\underline{v}|\), phir har component ko us se divide, aur aakhir mein check ke squares ka jama 1 aaye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\), yani \(x = 3\), \(y = -2\), \(z = 6\).
Humein find karna hai: \(|\underline{v}|\) aur \(\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma\).
Tareeqa: \(|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\). Direction cosines asal mein unit vector \(\underline{v}/|\underline{v}|\) ke components hi hain, is liye har component ko magnitude se divide karna kaafi hai.

Magnitude nikalein
\[|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{3^2 + (-2)^2 + 6^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{9 + 4 + 36}\]
\[= \sqrt{49} = 7\]
Kyun: Teen dimensions mein Pythagoras: har component ka square le kar jama kiya aur square root liya. Negative component ka square bhi positive hota hai, is liye sign ka koi asar nahi.

Har component ko \(|\underline{v}| = 7\) se divide karein
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{3}{7}\]
\[\cos\beta = \dfrac{-2}{7}\]
\[\cos\gamma = \dfrac{6}{7}\]
Kyun: Har axis ke saath ek right triangle banta hai jis ka hypotenuse vector ki lambai hai aur adjacent side wahi component. Cosine = adjacent / hypotenuse, is liye \(\cos\alpha = x/|\underline{v}|\). Sign bhi saath rahega: negative component ka matlab angle \(90^{\circ}\) se bara hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{9}{49} + \dfrac{4}{49} + \dfrac{36}{49}\]
\[= \dfrac{49}{49} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har vector ke liye \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\) hota hai (14.1.8 ka Important Result). Jama 1 aa gaya, is liye hamare direction cosines sahi hain.
blocks.final_answer:
\(|\underline{v}| = 7\); direction cosines \(\frac{3}{7}, -\frac{2}{7}, \frac{6}{7}\)
Negative \(\cos\beta\) batata hai ke vector y-axis se \(90^{\circ}\) se zyada angle banata hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find the magnitude of the vector \(\underline{v}\) and write the direction cosines of \(\underline{v}\): \(\underline{v} = -4\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do cheezein poochi gayi hain: vector \(\underline{v}\) ki lambai (magnitude) aur us ke direction cosines.
Direction cosines kya hain? Vector x, y aur z axes ke saath jo angles \(\alpha\), \(\beta\), \(\gamma\) banata hai, un ke cosines. Yeh batate hain ke vector kis taraf ishara kar raha hai.
Formula: \(\cos\alpha = x/|\underline{v}|\), \(\cos\beta = y/|\underline{v}|\), \(\cos\gamma = z/|\underline{v}|\).
Plan: pehle \(|\underline{v}|\), phir har component ko us se divide, aur aakhir mein check ke squares ka jama 1 aaye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{v} = -4\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\), yani \(x = -4\), \(y = 4\), \(z = 2\).
Humein find karna hai: \(|\underline{v}|\) aur \(\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma\).
Tareeqa: \(|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\). Direction cosines asal mein unit vector \(\underline{v}/|\underline{v}|\) ke components hi hain, is liye har component ko magnitude se divide karna kaafi hai.

Magnitude nikalein
\[|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + 4^2 + 2^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{16 + 16 + 4}\]
\[= \sqrt{36} = 6\]
Kyun: Teen dimensions mein Pythagoras: har component ka square le kar jama kiya aur square root liya. Negative component ka square bhi positive hota hai, is liye sign ka koi asar nahi.

Har component ko \(|\underline{v}| = 6\) se divide karein
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{-4}{6} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\]
\[\cos\beta = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
\[\cos\gamma = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: Har axis ke saath ek right triangle banta hai jis ka hypotenuse vector ki lambai hai aur adjacent side wahi component. Cosine = adjacent / hypotenuse, is liye \(\cos\alpha = x/|\underline{v}|\). Sign bhi saath rahega: negative component ka matlab angle \(90^{\circ}\) se bara hai. Phir fractions ko 2 se chhota kar ke lowest form mein likha.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{1}{9}\]
\[= \dfrac{9}{9} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har vector ke liye \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\) hota hai (14.1.8 ka Important Result). Jama 1 aa gaya, is liye hamare direction cosines sahi hain.
blocks.final_answer:
\(|\underline{v}| = 6\); direction cosines \(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{3}\)
Fractions ko hamesha lowest form mein likhiye.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Find the magnitude of the vector \(\underline{v}\) and write the direction cosines of \(\underline{v}\): \(\underline{v} = -6\underline{i} + 8\underline{j}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do cheezein poochi gayi hain: vector \(\underline{v}\) ki lambai (magnitude) aur us ke direction cosines.
Direction cosines kya hain? Vector x, y aur z axes ke saath jo angles \(\alpha\), \(\beta\), \(\gamma\) banata hai, un ke cosines. Yeh batate hain ke vector kis taraf ishara kar raha hai.
Formula: \(\cos\alpha = x/|\underline{v}|\), \(\cos\beta = y/|\underline{v}|\), \(\cos\gamma = z/|\underline{v}|\).
Plan: pehle \(|\underline{v}|\), phir har component ko us se divide, aur aakhir mein check ke squares ka jama 1 aaye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{v} = -6\underline{i} + 8\underline{j}\), yani \(x = -6\), \(y = 8\), \(z = 0\).
Humein find karna hai: \(|\underline{v}|\) aur \(\cos\alpha, \cos\beta, \cos\gamma\).
Tareeqa: \(|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\). Direction cosines asal mein unit vector \(\underline{v}/|\underline{v}|\) ke components hi hain, is liye har component ko magnitude se divide karna kaafi hai.

Magnitude nikalein
\[|\underline{v}| = \sqrt{(-6)^2 + 8^2 + 0^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{36 + 64 + 0}\]
\[= \sqrt{100} = 10\]
Kyun: Teen dimensions mein Pythagoras: har component ka square le kar jama kiya aur square root liya. Negative component ka square bhi positive hota hai, is liye sign ka koi asar nahi.

Har component ko \(|\underline{v}| = 10\) se divide karein
\[\cos\alpha = \dfrac{-6}{10} = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
\[\cos\beta = \dfrac{8}{10} = \dfrac{4}{5}\]
\[\cos\gamma = \dfrac{0}{10} = 0\]
Kyun: Har axis ke saath ek right triangle banta hai jis ka hypotenuse vector ki lambai hai aur adjacent side wahi component. Cosine = adjacent / hypotenuse, is liye \(\cos\alpha = x/|\underline{v}|\). Sign bhi saath rahega: negative component ka matlab angle \(90^{\circ}\) se bara hai. Yahan \(\underline{k}\) wala term likha hi nahi, iska matlab \(z = 0\) hai. Is liye \(\cos\gamma = 0\), yani \(\gamma = 90^{\circ}\).
Dhyan dein: missing component ko chhor dena ghalti hai; teesra direction cosine 0 zaroor likhiye.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{9}{25} + \dfrac{16}{25} + 0\]
\[= \dfrac{25}{25} = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Har vector ke liye \(\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1\) hota hai (14.1.8 ka Important Result). Jama 1 aa gaya, is liye hamare direction cosines sahi hain.
blocks.final_answer:
\(|\underline{v}| = 10\); direction cosines \(-\frac{3}{5}, \frac{4}{5}, 0\)
\(\cos\gamma = 0\) ka matlab \(\gamma = 90^{\circ}\): vector z-axis par perpendicular hai, yani xy-plane mein hai.
